summary: This bill increases the excise tax rate on the investment income of private colleges and universities from 1.4 percent to 10 percent, further raises it to 20 percent for institutions that increase their net price faster than inflation, and expands the number of institutions subject to this tax by lowering the asset threshold from $500,000 to $250,000 per student.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly modifies the excise tax on investment income of private colleges and universities, increasing the tax rate and expanding the institutions subject to it. This is the primary purpose of the bill.

The bill raises the excise tax rate on private college endowment income from 1.4% to 10% (or 20% for institutions raising net price faster than CPI) and expands the tax to more institutions. This generates additional federal revenue that would reduce the deficit, but the legislation's core purpose is higher-education accountability rather than fiscal consolidation, making the deficit impact tangential.
